title: The Secret Spy Network Feeding Russia’s War Machine

sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代冰淇淋。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最出色的球队。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于助您理解世界，充分过好每一天。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For years now, Russia's been the target of Western sanctions designed to keep it from building advanced weapons.
sentences.zh: 多年来，俄罗斯一直是西方制裁的目标，这些制裁旨在阻止其制造先进武器。

sentences.en: And yet, it's continued to batter Ukraine with high-tech missiles and drone attacks.
sentences.zh: 然而，它依然不断用高科技导弹和无人机袭击来重创乌克兰。

sentences.en: But how it's managed to do that has largely remained a mystery until now.
sentences.zh: 但它究竟是如何做到这一点的，直到现在基本上还是个谜。

sentences.en: Today, our colleague Jane Bradley explains what she's uncovered about the network of spies keeping the Kremlin's war machine running.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们的同事简·布拉德利将解释她所揭露的关于维持克里姆林宫战争机器运转的间谍网络内幕。

sentences.en: It's Friday, August 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月14日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jane Bradley, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 简·布拉德利，欢迎来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: So, Jane, I remember at the beginning of Russia's war with Ukraine, there were all of these
sentences.zh: 那么，简，我记得在俄罗斯与乌克兰战争刚开始的时候，有各种各样的

sentences.en: stories that basically made it seem like Russia was not equipped to wage a modern war, right?
sentences.zh: 报道基本上让人觉得俄罗斯根本没有能力打一场现代战争，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, they were rolling out these sort of mothballed Cold War-era tanks, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们拉出了那种封存的冷战时期的坦克之类的东西。

sentences.en: And yet, here we are, all these years later, and we're watching Russia continually hit Ukraine with these really sophisticated weapons.
sentences.zh: 然而，几年后的今天，我们却看到俄罗斯不断用这些非常先进的武器袭击乌克兰。

sentences.en: So, I guess my first question to you is, how have the Russians seemingly advanced so much from where they at least appeared to be when the war started?
sentences.zh: 所以，我想问你的第一个问题是，从战争刚开始时人们看到的状况来看，俄罗斯人怎么好像取得了这么大的进步？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a good question.
sentences.zh: 对，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, in the early days of the war, the old school equipment, the tanks you described, things like that, worked because it was largely an old school war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在战争初期，那些老式装备、你描述的坦克以及类似的东西之所以管用，是因为这基本上是一场老式战争。

sentences.en: Trench warfare between Ukrainian fighters and Russian forces as close as 15 feet apart.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰战士与俄罗斯军队之间的堑壕战，双方最近时只有15英尺的距离。

sentences.en: So, think soldiers with guns in trenches and bunkers.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以想象士兵们拿着枪在战壕和掩体里战斗。

sentences.en: The soldiers fire a rocket-propelled grenade.
sentences.zh: 士兵们发射火箭推进榴弹。

sentences.en: Often, they were separated by, you know, just a few hundred metres.
sentences.zh: 通常，他们相隔你知道的只有区区几百米。

sentences.en: But now there's a problem.
sentences.zh: 但现在出现了一个问题。

sentences.en: A Russian drone is overhead.
sentences.zh: 一架俄罗斯无人机正在头顶盘旋。

sentences.en: But over the last couple of years, the war in Ukraine has gone really high-tech.
sentences.zh: 但在过去几年里，乌克兰战争已经变得非常高科技。

sentences.en: This is what a kamikaze drone attack sounds like.
sentences.zh: 这就是神风特攻队式无人机袭击的声音。

sentences.en: Reports of waves of explosive-laden drones striking Kiev and setting residential buildings there on fire.
sentences.zh: 据报道，一波又一波载有炸药的无人机袭击了基辅，并点燃了那里的住宅楼。

sentences.en: Ukraine firing the first American-made long-range missiles into Russia.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰向俄罗斯发射了首批美国制造的远程导弹。

sentences.en: And it's shifted from artillery battles to drone warfare and ballistic missiles.
sentences.zh: 战局已经从炮兵战转向了无人机战和弹道导弹战。

sentences.en: And this is where Russia has a problem because it doesn't make this type of technology that it needs to build these kinds of high-tech weapons.
sentences.zh: 而这就是俄罗斯遇到问题的地方，因为它不生产制造这类高科技武器所需的这种技术。

sentences.en: And we're talking about things like semiconductors and microchips that act as the brain of drones and ballistic missiles and help direct them to their targets.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是半导体和微芯片之类东西，它们充当无人机和弹道导弹的大脑，并帮助引导它们飞向目标。

sentences.en: And in the early days of the war, Western countries, allies of Ukraine, imposed these sweeping trade restrictions,
sentences.zh: 在战争初期，西方国家、乌克兰的盟友实施了这些全面的贸易限制，

sentences.en: these sanctions designed to keep exactly this type of technology out of Russian hands.
sentences.zh: 这些制裁旨在将恰好这类技术彻底挡在俄罗斯人手之外。

sentences.en: And yet, obviously, those sanctions have not worked, right?
sentences.zh: 然而，显然这些制裁并没有起作用，对吧？

sentences.en: Because just in the past few months, we have seen Russia strike Kiev.
sentences.zh: 因为就在过去几个月里，我们看到俄罗斯打击了基辅。

sentences.en: It's struck other cities and towns inside Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 它打击了乌克兰境内的其他城市和城镇。

sentences.en: There have been these incredibly devastating consequences.
sentences.zh: 造成了这些令人难以置信的毁灭性后果。

sentences.en: Hundreds of civilians have died this year.
sentences.zh: 今年已有数百名平民丧生。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It hasn't worked.
sentences.zh: 它没有起作用。

sentences.en: So Ukraine has been investigating and trying to figure out how is Russia getting its hands on the technology, the parts it's supposed to be cut off from.
sentences.zh: 因此，乌克兰一直在调查并试图弄清楚，俄罗斯是如何弄到那些它本该被切断供应的技术和零部件的。

sentences.en: How does one even go about trying to trace the component parts of a missile or a drone and where they came from?
sentences.zh: 人们究竟该如何着手追溯导弹或无人机的零部件及其来源呢？

sentences.en: So every time there's a major attack in Ukraine, investigators from Ukraine's military intelligence service comb through.
sentences.zh: 因此，乌克兰每次在乌克兰境内遭受重大袭击时，乌克兰军方情报部门的调查人员都会进行彻底搜查。

sentences.en: They dig through recovered components from these weapons, these drones, these missiles.
sentences.zh: 他们从这些武器、无人机和导弹中搜寻并挖掘残存的零部件。

sentences.en: They're actually digging them out of the ground?
sentences.zh: 他们真的是从地里挖出来的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Literally combing through, digging it with their own hands.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上的搜寻，用他们自己的双手去挖。

sentences.en: And they're trying to find microchips and other weapons components.
sentences.zh: 他们正试图寻找微芯片和其他武器零部件。

sentences.en: And in 2024, these Ukrainian investigators started to notice something.
sentences.zh: 而在2024年，这些乌克兰调查人员开始注意到一些情况。

sentences.en: A lot of these weapons components that they were finding were actually coming from Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们发现的许多武器零部件实际上都来自日本。

sentences.en: And this was really surprising.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人吃惊。

sentences.en: Japan's been a close ally, a really vocal supporter of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 日本一直是乌克兰的亲密盟友和坚定支持者。

sentences.en: It was one of the first countries to issue sanctions against Russia on the very first day it invaded Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 它是在乌克兰遭到入侵的第一天就对俄罗斯实施制裁的首批国家之一。

sentences.en: And this really shocked and concerned the Ukrainian officials that I spoke to.
sentences.zh: 这确实让与我交谈过的乌克兰官员感到震惊和担忧。

sentences.en: And actually, when I first received a bunch of documents from Ukrainian sources, which included, you know, lists of this equipment, pictures of this equipment,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我第一次从乌克兰消息人士那里收到一堆文件时，其中包括这些设备的清单、这些设备的图片，

sentences.en: I was actually speaking to my source and asked, can you give me an idea of how many are being found on the battlefield in Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 我当时正在和我的消息人士交谈，并问他，你能让我大概了解一下在乌克兰战场上发现了多少这样的设备吗？

sentences.en: And he corrected me.
sentences.zh: 然后他纠正了我。

sentences.en: He was like, this is not the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 他说，这不是战场。

sentences.en: All of these parts are being found in civilian attacks.
sentences.zh: 所有这些零部件都是在针对平民的袭击中被发现的。

sentences.en: And in May, earlier this year, when these Ukrainian investigators were trawling through the debris of this awful attack on a residential building in Kyiv that had killed 24 people,
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候的5月，当这些乌克兰调查人员在清理基辅一栋住宅楼遭受可怕袭击后的废墟时，那场袭击夺去了24人的生命，

sentences.en: including children, they found Japanese components inside a missile that had destroyed the building.
sentences.zh: 其中包括儿童，他们在摧毁该建筑的一枚导弹内部发现了日本零部件。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And the Ukrainian government estimates that 90 percent of Russian weapons, drones, missiles contain Japanese components.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰政府估计，90%的俄罗斯武器、无人机和导弹都包含日本零部件。

sentences.en: So Japan is a critical supplier of the Russian war machine.
sentences.zh: 所以日本是俄罗斯战争机器的一个关键供应国。

sentences.en: OK, so clearly for the Ukrainians, the question is, if Japan has these sanctions,
sentences.zh: 好吧，对乌克兰人来说，显然问题在于，既然日本实施了这些制裁，

sentences.en: how are its parts nonetheless ending up in Russian weapons that are being used to attack its cities and its civilians?
sentences.zh: 为什么其零部件最终还是流向了被用来攻击其城市和平民的俄罗斯武器中？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: That's a question that Ukrainian investigators had.
sentences.zh: 这就是乌克兰调查人员心中的疑问。

sentences.en: That's a question we had when we first started reporting this story out.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们刚开始报道这个故事时心中的疑问。

sentences.en: Obviously, Japanese companies are banned from trading with Russia.
sentences.zh: 显然，日本公司被禁止与俄罗斯进行贸易。

sentences.en: So the question is, how are they getting around these export rules?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，它们是如何绕过这些出口规定的？

sentences.en: How is Russia getting its hands on these Japanese parts if it's not through legal routes?
sentences.zh: 如果不是通过合法途径，俄罗斯是怎么弄到这些日本零部件的？

sentences.en: How do you even begin to answer a question like that?
sentences.zh: 你甚至该如何着手回答这样一个问题？

sentences.en: So my colleagues and I, Michael Schwartz and Adam Goldman, started this investigation last year after we got a tip from an intelligence source.
sentences.zh: 因此，我的同事迈克尔·施瓦茨、亚当·戈德曼和我去年在收到一条情报线索后开始了这项调查。

sentences.en: And that tip eventually led to our conversations with five different Western intelligence agencies.
sentences.zh: 这条线索最终促成了我们与五个不同的西方情报机构的对话。

sentences.en: And what we found out is that the Russian intelligence service, the military service, the GIU,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，俄罗斯的情报机构、军事部门格鲁乌（GRU），

sentences.en: actually has a specialized spy unit that's entirely dedicated to evading Western sanctions and smuggling the parts, the technology that Russia needs for its war machine.
sentences.zh: 实际上拥有一个专门的间谍单位，完全致力于逃避西方制裁并走私俄罗斯战争机器所需的零部件和技术。

sentences.en: That unit is called the 20th directorate.
sentences.zh: 那个单位被称为第二0局。

sentences.en: And one of the big breakthroughs we got in our reporting was finally being able to identify the spy, the Russian spy leading its operations in Japan,
sentences.zh: 我们在报道中取得的一大突破，是最终能够确认在日开展行动的间谍、那名俄罗斯间谍的身份，

sentences.en: a guy by the name of Maxim Volchenkov.
sentences.zh: 一个名叫马克西姆·沃尔琴科夫的家伙。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So you are uncovering not just this secret, massive spy operation, the name of it, but you've actually gotten the name of one of the spies.
sentences.zh: 所以你们不仅揭露了这个秘密且庞大的间谍行动及其名称，而且你们还搞到了其中一名间谍的名字。

sentences.en: What do you know about him at this point?
sentences.zh: 目前你对他有什么了解？

sentences.en: So at this point, we know that he's a veteran GIU officer.
sentences.zh: 目前我们了解到他是一名资深的格鲁乌军官。

sentences.en: He's fluent in Japanese, Russian and English.
sentences.zh: 他精通日语、俄语和英语。

sentences.en: And he began his second tour of Japan back in 2024 when he was posted there on paper as an employee of Aeroflot, the Russian state airline.
sentences.zh: 他在2024年开始了他在日本的第二任期，当时他在纸面上被派驻到那里，身份是俄罗斯国有航空公司俄罗斯国际航空公司的员工。

sentences.en: So the cover for the spy, to be clear, is airline executive?
sentences.zh: 所以说清楚点，这个间谍的掩护身份是航空公司高管？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And what's interesting about that is in intelligence circles for years, Aeroflot has been known to be a cover for Russian spies, basically.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在情报界多年来，俄罗斯国际航空公司基本上一直被认为是用作俄罗斯间谍的掩护。

sentences.en: While also being a legitimate airline?
sentences.zh: 同时它也是一家合法的航空公司吗？

sentences.en: Like this thing is like a cover for spies, but also flies people, commercial?
sentences.zh: 就像这个东西既是间谍的掩护，但同时也运送商业旅客？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: So who knows who you could be sat next to?
sentences.zh: 所以谁知道你旁边坐的会是什么人呢？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So exciting.
sentences.zh: 太刺激了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And it's worth noting that Aeroflot is entirely state-owned.
sentences.zh: 值得一提的是，俄罗斯国际航空公司是完全国有的。

sentences.en: So Russian intelligence services have for years looked for state-owned entities that they basically control, where they can plant spies today, like Volchenkov.
sentences.zh: 因此，多年来俄罗斯情报机构一直在寻找他们基本能控制的国有实体，以便今天安插像沃尔琴科夫这样的间谍。

sentences.en: And what did you learn about what Volchenkov was doing under the cover of Aeroflot?
sentences.zh: 那么你们了解到沃尔琴科夫在俄罗斯国际航空公司的掩护下做了什么吗？

sentences.en: So we spoke to our Western intelligence sources to try and figure that out.
sentences.zh: 我们与我们的西方情报来源进行了交谈以试图弄清楚这一点。

sentences.en: And what they told us is that he was sent to Tokyo to basically develop relationships with a network of logistics companies, importers,
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们，他被派往东京，基本上是为了与一个物流公司和进口商网络建立关系，

sentences.en: that could be useful for them in smuggling these weapon parts to Russia.
sentences.zh: 这些公司可能对他们将这些武器零部件走私到俄罗斯大有帮助。

sentences.en: And what are these companies doing for Volchenkov exactly?
sentences.zh: 这些公司究竟在为沃尔琴科夫做什么？

sentences.en: Like, can you just explain that?
sentences.zh: 比如，你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So Volchenkov needs these companies to do a few things for him.
sentences.zh: 所以沃尔琴科夫需要这些公司为他做几件事。

sentences.en: The first thing is to actually buy the components that he needs.
sentences.zh: 第一件事是实际购买他需要的零部件。

sentences.en: Because of sanctions, Japanese companies are not allowed to sell these components to Russia or Russian companies right now.
sentences.zh: 由于制裁，日本公司目前不被允许向俄罗斯或俄罗斯公司出售这些零部件。

sentences.en: And so Volchenkov needs a middleman company to basically buy this equipment for him.
sentences.zh: 因此，沃尔琴科夫需要一家中间商公司来基本上帮他购买这些设备。

sentences.en: And then once he has the equipment, these components, he needs help shipping it out of Japan to Russia.
sentences.zh: 一旦他有了这些设备和零部件，他就需要有人帮忙将它们从日本运出并运往俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Why can't he just fly them, though, if he ostensibly works for Aeroflot?
sentences.zh: 不过，既然他表面上在俄罗斯国际航空公司工作，为什么他不能直接用飞机运走它们呢？

sentences.en: I mean, that would be a lot easier for him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那对他来说会容易得多。

sentences.en: But the sanctions imposed on Aeroflot by Japan and others means Aeroflot is effectively grounded in Japan.
sentences.zh: 但日本和其他国家对俄罗斯国际航空公司实施的制裁意味着，该航空公司实际上在日本被停飞了。

sentences.en: So they can't actually fly in and out of the country.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的飞机实际上无法飞进飞出该国。

sentences.en: And so Volchenkov needs to find these logistics companies in Japan who will essentially book passage for him on other airlines which are allowed to fly out of Japan.
sentences.zh: 因此，沃尔琴科夫需要在日本找到这些物流公司，由它们基本上为他在其他获准飞离日本的航空公司上预订舱位。

sentences.en: And because it's effectively illegal to fly this equipment directly to Russia,
sentences.zh: 而且由于将这些设备直接空运到俄罗斯实际上是非法的，

sentences.en: what these logistics companies will do is arrange transport from Japan to a third-party country like Sri Lanka or Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 这些物流公司会做的是安排从日本到斯里兰卡或越南等第三方国家的运输。

sentences.en: And then Aeroflot will charter one of their own planes from Vietnam or Sri Lanka, say, to get the goods from there to Russia.
sentences.zh: 然后俄罗斯国际航空公司将从越南或斯里兰卡包租他们自己的飞机之一，比方说，将货物从那里运到俄罗斯。

sentences.en: And so how is he identifying the kinds of companies that he can turn for Russian purposes?
sentences.zh: 那么他是如何识别出可以为俄罗斯目的所用的这类公司的呢？

sentences.en: So Volchenkov is part of a much wider network in the 20th Directorate.
sentences.zh: 沃尔琴科夫是第二0局更广泛网络的一部分。

sentences.en: And he will have GRU colleagues sat in Moscow at a desk who are looking for companies in Japan and elsewhere which could make good targets for Volchenkov to try and identify and build up relationships with.
sentences.zh: 他在莫斯科的办公室里会有格鲁乌同事坐在办公桌前，寻找日本及其他地方有可能成为沃尔琴科夫试图识别并建立关系的良好目标的公司。

sentences.en: And they tend to target these kind of mid-size logistics companies, small or mid-size, ones that don't attract much attention.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会把目标锁定在这些中小型物流公司上，小型或中型，那些不太引人注目的公司。

sentences.en: Which are registered in Japan, but they tend to have someone Russian in a senior position.
sentences.zh: 这些公司在在日本注册，但往往在高级职位上有一个俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: Wait, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 等等，不好意思。

sentences.en: How big is the universe of obscure Japanese companies run by Russians who are sympathetic to the Kremlin?
sentences.zh: 由对克里姆林宫有好感的俄罗斯人经营的不起眼的日本公司的总体规模有多大？

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Way, way too big as I found out at this stage of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 正如我在报道的这个阶段所发现的，实在是大得离谱。

sentences.en: But what was helpful is that if you go on the Aeroflot website, they list their official partners in every country.
sentences.zh: 但有帮助的是，如果你访问俄罗斯国际航空公司的网站，他们会列出他们在每个国家的官方合作伙伴。

sentences.en: So we had the names of two logistics companies.
sentences.zh: 所以我们掌握了两家物流公司的名称。

sentences.en: And then when I looked through the corporate filings, I found that lo and behold,
sentences.zh: 然后，当我翻阅公司注册文件时，我发现不出所料，

sentences.en: there was a senior Russian in each company or a Japanese business person with strong connections to Russia, which is kind of the wider profile they're looking at.
sentences.zh: 每家公司都有一名资深俄罗斯人，或者与俄罗斯有着紧密联系的日本商人，这正是他们寻找的更广泛的画像。

sentences.en: So that gave us a really good lead.
sentences.zh: 这为我们提供了非常好的线索。

sentences.en: And then we took the names of those companies back to our intelligence sources and asked them, are these companies worth digging into?
sentences.zh: 然后我们将这些公司的名字带回给我们的情报源，并问他们，这些公司值得深入挖掘吗？

sentences.en: And they basically said yes.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上回答说值得。

sentences.en: But just to go back to the spy Volchenkov for a second.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们先回到间谍沃尔琴科夫身上。

sentences.en: If all of these places are involved in the supply chain, like Vietnam, Sri Lanka, as you mentioned, is there a reason that he's in Japan specifically?
sentences.zh: 既然所有这些地方都卷入了供应链，比如越南、斯里兰卡，正如你所提到的，他为什么偏偏要去日本？

sentences.en: Because, again, Japan is a Western ally.
sentences.zh: 因为同样，日本是西方盟友。

sentences.en: So he's in Japan for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以他去日本有两个原因。

sentences.en: One is that Japan makes the high-tech technology that Russia needs.
sentences.zh: 一个原因是日本制造俄罗斯所需的高精尖技术。

sentences.en: And sure, China makes some of it, some of the microchips, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 当然，中国也制造其中的一部分，比如一些微芯片等等。

sentences.en: But Japan really specializes in particular machine tools, things that drill, that cut, that they basically need to make these parts for Russian weapons.
sentences.zh: 但日本真正擅长的是特定的机床，也就是用于钻孔、切割的设备，这些正是制造俄军武器零部件所必不可少的。

sentences.en: And the second thing is that Japan is known and has been for years as a spy paradise.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因是，日本众所周知并且多年来一直是间谍天堂。

sentences.en: So, Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以，日本。

sentences.en: Japan is a spy paradise.
sentences.zh: 日本是个间谍天堂。

sentences.en: And it has this long history of that, dating back to World War II, when its once kind of fierce intelligence capabilities were dismantled by the war's winners, the Americans.
sentences.zh: 而且它有着悠久的历史，可以追溯到二战时期，当时它一度堪称凶猛的情报能力被战争的胜利者——美国人解体了。

sentences.en: And it's never really recovered since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，它就再也没有真正恢复过。

sentences.en: You know, it has no foreign intelligence agency at all.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它根本没有外国情报机构。

sentences.en: In fact, it doesn't have any centralized intelligence agency.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它没有任何中央情报机构。

sentences.en: It's kind of split between these five, six different departments within different government agencies.
sentences.zh: 它大体上被分拆在不同政府机构底下的这五六个不同部门中。

sentences.en: So to answer your question, Japan has the technology that Russia needs.
sentences.zh: 所以回答你的问题，日本拥有俄罗斯需要的技术。

sentences.en: And it's much easier for Russian spies to operate and base themselves from Japan.
sentences.zh: 而且俄罗斯间谍要在日本活动并把总部设在那里要容易得多。

sentences.en: And it's not just Volchenkov.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是沃尔琴科夫（Volchenkov）。

sentences.en: Our sources told us that dozens of Russian spies fled to Japan as Europe and the West expelled hundreds as Russia invaded Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我们的消息人士告诉我们，随着俄罗斯入侵乌克兰，欧洲和西方驱逐了数百名俄罗斯人，数十名俄罗斯间谍逃往了日本。

sentences.en: They found a safe haven in Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们在日本找到了一个避难所。

sentences.en: Okay, so clearly very easy to be a spy in Japan is what you're telling us.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以显然你的意思是，在日本当间谍非常容易。

sentences.en: So at this point, Jane, you have a name, Volchenkov.
sentences.zh: 简（Jane），那么现在你掌握了一个名字，沃尔琴科夫。

sentences.en: You've identified some of the Japanese companies working with him.
sentences.zh: 你已经确认了一些与他合作的日本公司。

sentences.en: What do you do next?
sentences.zh: 接下来你做什么？

sentences.en: It's one thing to have a bunch of information from anonymous intelligence sources, but we needed to prove or at least corroborate what they told us ourselves.
sentences.zh: 从匿名情报来源获得一堆信息是一回事，但我们需要自己去证明或至少证实他们告诉我们的内容。

sentences.en: So the next thing we did was hunt for addresses for Volchenkov, for the network of logistic companies we've been told is helping him.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做的下一件事就是搜寻沃尔琴科夫的地址，以及我们被告知正在协助他的物流公司网络的地址。

sentences.en: And my aim was to try and speak with Volchenkov and as many of those business owners as possible to try and find out what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我的目的是设法与沃尔琴科夫以及尽可能多的这些企业主谈谈，以弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And so I booked my tickets to Tokyo in the hope that I could get some of them to talk to me.
sentences.zh: 所以我预订了去东京的机票，希望我能让其中一些人跟我谈谈。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So Jane, at this point, you are headed to Tokyo, you're on the trail of this Russian spy.
sentences.zh: 简，那么现在你正前往东京，你正在追踪这个俄罗斯间谍。

sentences.en: What's the protocol for something like this?
sentences.zh: 像这种情况的规程是什么？

sentences.en: Like, can you just knock on his door like any other source?
sentences.zh: 比如说，你可以像敲其他消息人士的门一样直接去敲他的门吗？

sentences.en: I'm not sure there is a protocol for trying to hunt down a GIU officer in Japan.
sentences.zh: 我不确定在日本试图追查一名俄罗斯格鲁乌（GRU）军官是否有固定的规程。

sentences.en: I didn't know of one.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有什么规程。

sentences.en: And honestly, I had no idea what to expect.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我根本不知道会遇到什么。

sentences.en: And when I got there, Volchenkov was the first person on my list, obviously, to try and get to speak to me.
sentences.zh: 当我到达那里时，沃尔琴科夫显然是我名单上的第一个人，我试图去跟他谈谈。

sentences.en: So I rocked up at the Aeroflot office with my translator.
sentences.zh: 所以我带着我的译者大摇大摆地来到了俄罗斯国际航空公司（Aeroflot）的办公室。

sentences.en: It's like a sparkling 22-storey plus tower block by this old shrine.
sentences.zh: 它就像是一座矗立在古老神社旁、闪闪发光的22层以上的高楼大厦。

sentences.en: And we just walked in.
sentences.zh: 我们就这样走了进去。

sentences.en: We just walked in.
sentences.zh: 我们就这样走了进去。

sentences.en: It was this huge...
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的……

sentences.en: You didn't get stopped by security.
sentences.zh: 你没有被保安拦下吗？

sentences.en: There was no security.
sentences.zh: 那里没有保安。

sentences.en: There was no reception desk.
sentences.zh: 没有接待台。

sentences.en: I guess Tokyo is such a safe city that you can just walk straight into the lift, go up to the 22nd floor.
sentences.zh: 我想东京是一座如此安全的城市，以至于你可以直接走进电梯，上到22层。

sentences.en: And the doors opened.
sentences.zh: 门打开了。

sentences.en: And I was taken by surprise because the Aeroflot office door is literally right there.
sentences.zh: 我感到很意外，因为俄罗斯国际航空公司的办公室大门就 literalmente（字面意思）在那里。

sentences.en: Well, and I knocked on the door and a middle-aged woman with a Russian Orthodox cross around her neck answered the door.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我敲了门，一个脖子上戴着东正教十字架的中年妇女开门了。

sentences.en: She looked really surprised to see me.
sentences.zh: 看到我她显得非常惊讶。

sentences.en: So I just introduced myself with my name and asked if Mr. Volchenkov was in the office.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是报上自己的名字做了解释，并询问沃尔琴科夫先生是否在办公室。

sentences.en: She, again, still looking quite surprised, said he wasn't and that we would need to make an appointment.
sentences.zh: 她依然显得相当惊讶，说他不在，我们需要预约。

sentences.en: And over the next three days, we were in this kind of almost comedy-like cat-and-mouse chase with him.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的三天里，我们和他展开了一场几乎像喜剧一样的猫鼠游戏。

sentences.en: So every time we knocked, she would say, come back at this time.
sentences.zh: 所以每次我们去敲门，她就会说，在这个时间回来。

sentences.en: I would come back at that time.
sentences.zh: 我就会在那个时间回来。

sentences.en: He's not now at the office.
sentences.zh: 他现在不在办公室。

sentences.en: He's not at the office.
sentences.zh: 他不在办公室。

sentences.en: She kept telling us he wasn't around and then it got to the day before my flight.
sentences.zh: 她一直告诉我们他不在附近，然后就到了我航班起飞的前一天。

sentences.en: Sorry to bother you.
sentences.zh: 打扰一下。

sentences.en: I have to fly back tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我明天得飞回去。

sentences.en: I just wanted to see if Mr. Volchenkov...
sentences.zh: 我只是想看看沃尔琴科夫先生……

sentences.en: I'd said, please, can we speak to Mr. Volchenkov?
sentences.zh: 我说过，求求你，我们能和沃尔琴科夫先生谈谈吗？

sentences.en: I should ask him.
sentences.zh: 我应该去问问他。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And she says, I'm sorry, Mr. Volchenkov never wants to speak with you.
sentences.zh: 然后她说，很抱歉，沃尔琴科夫先生永远不想跟你们谈话。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Rude.
sentences.zh: 太粗鲁了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Rude.
sentences.zh: 太粗鲁了。

sentences.en: There was no pretense at that point.
sentences.zh: 那时候已经没有任何伪装了。

sentences.en: I've come back another time.
sentences.zh: 我又去了一次。

sentences.en: And we never got in front of him, despite us trying to contact him for three days and him having our numbers and clearly knew who we were.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们试图联系他三天，而且他有我们的电话号码、显然也知道我们是谁，但我们始终没能见到他。

sentences.en: But we then set off on the trail of trying to track down business associates who had met him and did know what he was doing at Aeroflot.
sentences.zh: 但随后我们踏上了追寻那些曾与他会面、且确实知道他在俄罗斯国际航空公司做什么的商业伙伴的足迹。

sentences.en: And how did that go?
sentences.zh: 那进展如何？

sentences.en: So one of the people we knew that Volchenkov worked with was a guy called Takahiko Miki.
sentences.zh: 我们知道与沃尔琴科夫合作过的人之一是一个名叫三木隆彦（Takahiko Miki）的家伙。

sentences.en: And he was the owner of a company called Proko Air, which is this logistics company which helps organize cargo getting from A to B.
sentences.zh: 他是Proko Air公司的老板，这是一家帮助安排货物从A点运到B点的物流公司。

sentences.en: And we tracked him down to this high rise in Tokyo's industrial port neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我们在东京工业港口附近的一栋高楼里找到了他。

sentences.en: And his wife answered the door and they eventually invited us in.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子开了门，他们最终邀请我们进去。

sentences.en: And when you walk in, you see these model planes.
sentences.zh: 当你走进去时，你会看到这些飞机模型。

sentences.en: There was an Aeroflot plane.
sentences.zh: 有一架俄罗斯国际航空公司的飞机。

sentences.en: There was a certificate to Proko Air for its excellent service to Aeroflot.
sentences.zh: 有一张颁发给Proko Air的证书，表彰其为俄罗斯国际航空公司提供的卓越服务。

sentences.en: And we followed him into his own office, this kind of dim, windowless room.
sentences.zh: 我们跟着他进入了他自己的办公室，这是一个光线昏暗、没有窗户的房间。

sentences.en: And he's really not what you would imagine someone accused of helping a Russian spy procure sanctioned goods to Russia would look like.
sentences.zh: 他实在不像是那种你想象中会被指控帮助俄罗斯间谍向俄罗斯采购受制裁物资的人。

sentences.en: He's got this real earnest manner.
sentences.zh: 他有一种非常真诚的举止。

sentences.en: And sources had described him to me as this kind of teddy bear-like figure.
sentences.zh: 消息人士曾向我形容他是一个有点像泰迪熊的人物。

sentences.en: And that is how he comes across.
sentences.zh: 他给人的感觉确实如此。

sentences.en: He seemed like he really wanted to help and he answered all my questions.
sentences.zh: 他看起来真的很想帮忙，并回答了我所有的提问。

sentences.en: And he really just was very insistent that, yes, he works with Aeroflot.
sentences.zh: 他非常坚持地表示，是的，他与俄罗斯国际航空公司合作。

sentences.en: Yes, he works with Volchenkov.
sentences.zh: 是的，他与沃尔琴科夫合作。

sentences.en: But no, he does not ship any sanctioned goods to Russia and that he would never do that.
sentences.zh: 但是不，他没有向俄罗斯运送任何受制裁的物资，而且他绝不会做那种事。

sentences.en: So what is he telling you that he's shipping?
sentences.zh: 那他跟你说他在运送什么？

sentences.en: If he's being so open about the fact that he actually ships stuff?
sentences.zh: 如果他对于自己确实在运送货物这件事表现得如此坦诚的话？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So he claimed that he only ships medical equipment and a few cosmetics.
sentences.zh: 所以他声称自己只运送医疗设备和少量化妆品。

sentences.en: And there are exemptions allowed for medical equipment, sanctioned carve-outs.
sentences.zh: 而且医疗设备是有豁免权的，属于受制裁的豁免范围。

sentences.en: So he said that this was all above board.
sentences.zh: 所以他说这一切都是完全合规的。

sentences.en: There is no way he would ship sanctioned goods or his business would shut down.
sentences.zh: 他绝不可能运送受制裁的物资，否则他的公司就会倒闭。

sentences.en: And honestly, like, I don't think I'm gullible or naive.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我觉得自己并不轻信或天真。

sentences.en: But he did come across as very earnest and almost convincing in that I could imagine him being a bit negligent
sentences.zh: 但他确实显得非常真诚，甚至很有说服力，以至于我可以想象他可能有点疏忽大意

sentences.en: and not carrying out the checks, the due diligence checks he should have done.
sentences.zh: 而没有进行本该进行的检查，即尽职调查检查。

sentences.en: How is that possible, though, exactly?
sentences.zh: 但这到底是怎么可能的呢？

sentences.en: Like, you said that maybe he's not doing his due diligence, but, like, how would he not know what he's shipping, basically?
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，也许他没有做好尽职调查，但是，他怎么可能基本上连自己在运送什么都不知道呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And I guess I've reported on sanctions, Russian sanctions for years.
sentences.zh: 我想我报道过制裁，即针对俄罗斯的制裁多年了。

sentences.en: And one of the defenses I would often hear is that, oh, we didn't know Russia was the final destination, right?
sentences.zh: 我经常听到的辩解之一就是，哦，我们不知道俄罗斯是最终目的地，对吧？

sentences.en: We thought this was just going to Vietnam or Sri Lanka.
sentences.zh: 我们以为这只是运往越南或斯里兰卡的。

sentences.en: And then the other defense is that, oh, I just took the paperwork at face value and I didn't know these were actually sanctioned goods and the paperwork was all bogus.
sentences.zh: 然后另一种辩解是，哦，我只是按字面意思接受了文件，我不知道这些其实是受制裁的物资，而且文件全是伪造的。

sentences.en: And one of the defenses he relied on was just like, I'm just booking cargo space, right, on these planes.
sentences.zh: 他依赖的辩解之一就类似于：我只是在预订货舱空间，对吧，在这些飞机上。

sentences.en: I'm not the manufacturer.
sentences.zh: 我不是制造商。

sentences.en: I'm not the supplier.
sentences.zh: 我不是供应商。

sentences.en: And I played a little dumb and asked him if he could show me an example of an invoice.
sentences.zh: 我装作有点愚笨，问他能不能给我看一个发票的例子。

sentences.en: And he then gestures to his wife to fetch the nearest invoice from the top of a pile in the office.
sentences.zh: 然后他示意他的妻子去拿办公室里一堆文件最上面的那张发票。

sentences.en: He brings it back to me.
sentences.zh: 他把它拿回来交给我。

sentences.en: And before he gives it to me, he attempts to redact identifying information.
sentences.zh: 在他把它交给我之前，他试图涂黑那些可以识别身份的信息。

sentences.en: So who's shipping it?
sentences.zh: 到底是谁在发货？

sentences.en: But what do you mean redact?
sentences.zh: 但你说的涂黑是什么意思？

sentences.en: Like he's just striking things out with a pen?
sentences.zh: 就像他是用笔把东西划掉吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: He just got a black marker pen and crossed out the details he didn't want me to see.
sentences.zh: 他只是拿了一支黑色马克笔，把那些他不想让我看到的细节划掉了。

sentences.en: And I left that interview with that piece of paper in my hand.
sentences.zh: 我手里拿着那张纸离开了那次采访。

sentences.en: And when I got back to the hotel and held it up to the light, the redactions didn't work.
sentences.zh: 当我回到酒店把它对着光举起来时，涂黑根本没用。

sentences.en: You could completely see who, who the receiver, who he was shipping this equipment to.
sentences.zh: 你可以完全看清是谁，收货人是谁，他究竟把这些设备运给了谁。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: Honestly, it was one of those reporting breakthrough moments that is really exciting.
sentences.zh: 老实说，那是那种令人兴奋的报道突破时刻之一。

sentences.en: What did you see?
sentences.zh: 你看到了什么？

sentences.en: Where was he shipping it to once you held it up to the light?
sentences.zh: 当你把它对着光举起来时，他到底是把它运到哪里去了？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I could see that the company he was supplying, that he was shipping to, was a Russian pharmaceutical company called R-Pharm.
sentences.zh: 对，所以我可以看到他正在供应、正在发货的公司是一家名为R-Pharm的俄罗斯制药公司。

sentences.en: And its founder had actually been sanctioned by the UK, by Canada, by Australia for his extensive ties to Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 其创始人实际上因与弗拉基米尔·普京有着广泛的联系而受到了英国、加拿大、澳大利亚的制裁。

sentences.en: Wait, OK, so does that mean that when you were in his office, he was lying to you and he said, oh, I don't know what's in it.
sentences.zh: 等等，好吧，那是不是意味着当你在他办公室里时，他对你撒了谎，他说，哦，我不知道里面装的是什么。

sentences.en: And what I do know, it's all legal and above board.
sentences.zh: 而且据我所知，这一切都是合法且合规的。

sentences.en: That's what the evidence suggests.
sentences.zh: 证据就是这么显示的。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And when I got back from Tokyo,
sentences.zh: 当我从东京回来后，

sentences.en: we actually spoke to two people who told us that Mr. Miki had specifically asked for help shipping prohibited items that he acknowledged were banned from being exported to Russia.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上与两个人进行了交谈，他们告诉我们，三木先生曾明确请求帮助运送违禁物品，而他承认这些物品是被禁止出口到俄罗斯的。

sentences.en: OK, so maybe not just a guy who was negligent with his paperwork.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他可能不仅仅是一个对文件疏忽大意的人。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: I want to go back to how this whole reporting journey started, because if you are able to piece this together, the Western intelligence sources that tipped you off,
sentences.zh: 我想回到这篇报道的整个历程是如何开始的，因为如果你能把这些拼凑起来，那些向你通风报信的西方情报来源，

sentences.en: presumably they knew all of this already, right?
sentences.zh: 想必他们早就知道这一切了，对吧？

sentences.en: Why did they tip you off in the first place?
sentences.zh: 他们当初为什么要向你通风报信？

sentences.en: Like, what did they need from you?
sentences.zh: 比如说，他们从你这里需要什么？

sentences.en: They tipped us off in the first place because they were both baffled and frustrated about Japan's lack of response.
sentences.zh: 他们当初向我们通风报信，是因为他们对日本的不作为既感到困惑又感到沮丧。

sentences.en: So let's be clear, both Ukrainian officials and foreign governments had warned Japan that this was happening,
sentences.zh: 所以我们要明确一点，乌克兰官员和外国政府都曾警告过日本这正在发生，

sentences.en: that Russian intelligence officers were operating in Tokyo and procuring this Japanese technology and that this Japanese technology was repeatedly being found on the battlefield in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 警告俄罗斯情报官员正在东京活动并采购这些日本技术，而且这些日本技术屡次在乌克兰战场上被发现。

sentences.en: And it being used in civilian attacks.
sentences.zh: 并且被用于针对平民的袭击中。

sentences.en: Ukraine is basically telling Japan everything that Ukraine thinks it needs to know to take some kind of action.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰基本上是在把乌克兰认为需要了解的一切都告诉日本，以便日本采取某种行动。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: They think they could take action to cut off the supply of Japanese parts to Russia if there was the political will to do so.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，如果有采取行动的政治意愿，日本是可以采取行动切断对俄日本零部件供应的。

sentences.en: So I spoke to a Ukrainian official who said that in the early days of the war, they were finding a lot of parts from Germany in Russian weapons,
sentences.zh: 所以我采访了一位乌克兰官员，他说在战争初期，他们在俄罗斯武器中发现了很多来自德国的零部件，

sentences.en: up to 20% actually in the early days.
sentences.zh: 在早期甚至高达20%。

sentences.en: And they warned the Germans and Germany almost immediately cut off the supply of German components to Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们警告了德国，德国几乎立即切断了对俄德国零部件的供应。

sentences.en: And Japan hasn't done the same.
sentences.zh: 而日本却没有这样做。

sentences.en: So that's one example that they pointed to say, if the political will is there, they can choke the supply chain.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是他们指出的一个例子，意思是，如果政治意愿具备，他们是可以卡住供应链的。

sentences.en: But Japan has not done that.
sentences.zh: 但日本并没有这样做。

sentences.en: But as you pointed out, Jane, Japan does not have the intelligence apparatus that Germany does, right?
sentences.zh: 但正如你所指出的，简，日本并没有德国那样强大的情报机构，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's what's made them, as you have explained, this spy paradise, for lack of a better term.
sentences.zh: 正如你所解释的，这也正是让他们成为所谓的“间谍天堂”的原因。

sentences.en: So where does Japan stand on this sort of bigger problem of not having that intelligence operation that they might need to counter all of this?
sentences.zh: 那么，在缺乏应对这一切所需的情报行动这一更大的问题上，日本的立场是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the first thing to say is that Japan acknowledges it has a problem when it comes to espionage right now, today.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为首先要说的是，日本承认它现在、今天在间谍活动方面确实存在问题。

sentences.en: And actually, when I sat down and talked with a senior lawmaker in Japan's government and asked about what they knew about the spies operating in Japan, he said that, look,
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我坐下来与日本政府的一位高级议员交谈，询问他们对在日本活动的间谍了解多少时，他说，你看，

sentences.en: we have a sense of crisis about the situation.
sentences.zh: 我们对目前的局势有一种危机感。

sentences.en: We don't have an exact number on the spies operating in Japan, in Tokyo, but we know there are a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们无法给出在日本东京活动的间谍的确切数字，但我们知道有很多。

sentences.en: And more broadly, Prime Minister Takeichi is really trying to build up Japan's intelligence capabilities.
sentences.zh: 更广泛地说，高市首相确实在极力建立日本的情报能力。

sentences.en: She's trying to build, under this new legislation that's being passed, Japan's first centralized intelligence agency.
sentences.zh: 她正试图在正在通过的新立法下，建立日本第一个中央情报机构。

sentences.en: But if it succeeds, if Japan succeeds, this is going to be a long-term project and not something that is going to happen overnight.
sentences.zh: 但如果成功了，如果日本成功了，这将是一个长期的项目，而不是一夜之间就能实现的事情。

sentences.en: How does this get solved then?
sentences.zh: 那这到底该怎么解决呢？

sentences.en: Like, where does that leave everything?
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这会让局面变成什么样？

sentences.en: Well, in the days after we published our investigation, we heard from sources that the Japanese government had begun investigating Philchenkov and Mr. Miki of Prokowa,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在我们发表调查报道后的几天里，我们从消息人士那里听说，日本政府已经开始调查菲利琴科夫和普罗科瓦的米基先生，

sentences.en: and were kind of looking into what was going on here.
sentences.zh: 并且正在着手调查这里究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: And we got some news recently that Philchenkov, the GIU spy, has actually fled Japan the day after we published our story.
sentences.zh: 我们最近得到消息称，GRU间谍菲利琴科夫在我们发表报道的第二天就已经逃离了日本。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it seems like putting the spotlight on him and this wider problem Japan has, has had the effect that our sources wanted it to, in that Philchenkov has been bent.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以看起来把聚光灯对准他以及日本面临的这个更广泛的问题，起到了我们消息人士所希望的效果，因为菲利琴科夫的身份已经暴露了。

sentences.en: His identity is now out there.
sentences.zh: 他的身份现在已经大白于天下。

sentences.en: And Japan seems to have been embarrassed into some kind of action, though we need to spend a bit more time watching it to see how substantive that is.
sentences.zh: 而且日本似乎在尴尬之余采取了某种行动，尽管我们需要花更多时间来观察其实际力度有多大。

sentences.en: Basically, this guy's cover was blown, so he can't really act like a spy anymore.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这家伙的掩护被彻底戳穿了，所以他再也不能像个间谍一样行事了。

sentences.en: He flees.
sentences.zh: 他逃跑了。

sentences.en: I wonder, Jane, where does his departure leave this giant sanctions-busting operation that he's helped set up,
sentences.zh: 简，我很好奇，他的离开对由他协助建立的这个庞大的规避制裁行动意味着什么，

sentences.en: like the supply chain that has been very well underway funneling parts to Russia?
sentences.zh: 比如那条一直源源不断向俄罗斯输送零部件的供应链？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think Philchenkov's an important player for Russia for the 20th directorate, but he's still only one player.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为菲利琴科夫对俄罗斯第二十局来说是个重要的棋子，但他终究只是一个棋子。

sentences.en: So him fleeing has definitely made it harder for Russia to get the technology it needs from Japan, but there are many other players.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的逃跑确实让俄罗斯从日本获取所需技术变得更加困难，但还有许多其他棋子。

sentences.en: We know there are dozens of Russian spies in Japan alone, so there will be others that can take his place.
sentences.zh: 我们知道仅在日本就有几十名俄罗斯间谍，所以还会有其他人来取代他的位置。

sentences.en: So unless something drastically changed in Japan, whether it's the espionage laws, whether it's a crackdown on the manufacturers, the companies that are part of this supply chain,
sentences.zh: 因此，除非日本发生根本性的巨变，无论是反间谍法，还是对构成这条供应链的制造商和企业的打击，

sentences.en: then somebody else is just going to pop up and replace Philchenkov, and the supply chain will continue.
sentences.zh: 否则就会有其他人冒出来取代菲利琴科夫，供应链也将继续运转。

sentences.en: I wonder, Jane, let's just say that Japan is able to crack down on all of this and does so tomorrow, expels all the spies, stops the technology, ends everything.
sentences.zh: 简，我想知道，假设日本能够打击这一切并且明天就付诸行动，驱逐所有间谍，阻止技术输出，终结一切。

sentences.en: How meaningful would that actually be to Russia's war effort in Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 这对于俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争努力究竟有多大意义？

sentences.en: It would be incredibly meaningful.
sentences.zh: 那将具有极其重大的意义。

sentences.en: The pipeline of these Japanese components to Russia is absolutely essential for Putin to keep waging his war against Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这些日本零部件流向俄罗斯的生命线，对于普京维持对乌克兰的战争绝对至关重要。

sentences.en: If that supply was cut off, Russia would not be able to maintain its weapons to build new weapons, particularly, you know, drones, ballistic missiles,
sentences.zh: 如果切断了这条供应，俄罗斯将无法维护其武器，也无法制造新武器，尤其是你知道的，无人机、弹道导弹，

sentences.en: all this high-tech equipment that the war has now become more dependent on.
sentences.zh: 以及这场战争现在越来越依赖的所有这些高科技装备。

sentences.en: So Japan's playing a really high-stakes game here.
sentences.zh: 所以日本在这里玩的是一场赌注极高的游戏。

sentences.en: If Japan takes meaningful action in a way that is bigger than just one spy, however important he is, fleeing Japan,
sentences.zh: 如果日本采取有意义的行动，其力度超越单纯针对某个间谍（无论他多么重要）逃离日本这件事，

sentences.en: it has this real opportunity to change the course of a war that has raged on for four years now.
sentences.zh: 它就拥有了一个真正的机会去改变一场已经持续了四年的战争的进程。

sentences.en: The question now is whether Japan's going to take the chance to do that.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，日本是否会抓住这个机会去这样做。

sentences.en: Jane, I have to ask, now that Philchenkov's cover has been blown, what does he do now?
sentences.zh: 简，我不得不问，既然菲利琴科夫的掩护已经暴露，他现在该怎么办？

sentences.en: What can a spy do once everybody knows who they are?
sentences.zh: 当所有人都知道他是谁之后，一个间谍还能做些什么？

sentences.en: Well, he's almost certainly back in Russia and his foreign intelligence career is without a doubt over.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他几乎可以肯定已经回到了俄罗斯，而且他的外国情报生涯无疑已经结束了。

sentences.en: You know, his face is out there.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他的脸已经曝光了。

sentences.en: His name is out there.
sentences.zh: 他的名字已经人尽皆知了。

sentences.en: He won't be able to work as a spy abroad again.
sentences.zh: 他将无法再在海外从事间谍工作。

sentences.en: What often happens with these spies whose covers are blown is that they get a hero's welcome back in Russia.
sentences.zh: 这些掩护被暴露的间谍通常会遭遇这样的情况：他们在俄罗斯受到英雄般的欢迎。

sentences.en: Often they get a medal or they get appointed to a spy school to train the next generations.
sentences.zh: 通常他们会获得一枚勋章，或者被任命到间谍学校去培训下一代。

sentences.en: So the cycle starts again.
sentences.zh: 于是，这个循环又开始了。

sentences.en: Jane Bradley, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 简·布拉德利，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来，蕾切尔。

sentences.en: Jane Bradley, she's an investigative reporter for The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 简·布拉德利，她是《纽约时报》的调查记者。

sentences.en: And you can get even more reporting, Jane Bradley's reporting, other people throughout the newsroom, by downloading the New York Times app.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过下载《纽约时报》应用程序，获取更多简·布拉德利以及新闻室其他同仁的报道。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, we want to mention right now, you can download the app and get one month of completely free access to everything in there.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订户，我们现在想提醒你，你可以下载该应用程序，并获得一个月完全免费访问其中所有内容的权限。

sentences.en: Download it and we'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 下载它，我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: The judge said the anti-Semitic incidents cited by the administration were, quote, too isolated and episodic to show that Harvard was breaking the law.
sentences.zh: 法官表示，政府所引用的反犹太事件“过于孤立和零星，不足以证明哈佛违反了法律”。

sentences.en: And the board of the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C., voted on Thursday to put President Trump's name back on the side of the building, beneath the main sign.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿特区肯尼迪中心董事会于周四投票决定，将特朗普总统的名字重新加回到大楼侧面、主标牌下方。

sentences.en: That's according to two people with knowledge of the matter.
sentences.zh: 这是根据两位知情人士透露的消息。

sentences.en: The president's name had been added to the building last year, but a judge had ordered that it be taken down,
sentences.zh: 总统的名字去年曾被添加到大楼上，但一名法官下令将其拆除，

sentences.en: finding that only Congress had the authority to change the institution's name.
sentences.zh: 裁定只有国会有权更改该机构的名称。

sentences.en: The move by the Trump-aligned board of the Kennedy Center is an aggressive test of the judge's decision.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪中心亲特朗普董事会的这一举动是对法官裁决的一次挑衅性试探。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Shannon Lin, Jessica Chung, and Olivia Natt, with help from Adrienne HurSt.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由香农·林、杰西卡·钟和奥利维亚·纳特制作，阿德里安·赫斯特提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Annie Minoff, with help from Maria Byrne, Chris Haxel, and Michael Benoit.
sentences.zh: 节目由安妮·米诺夫剪辑，玛丽亚·伯恩、克里斯·哈克塞尔和迈克尔·勒努瓦提供了帮助。

sentences.en: Contains music by Alicia Ba'itup, Diane Wong, Dan Powell, and Pat McCusker.
sentences.zh: 包含由艾丽西亚·拜伊图普、黛安·王、丹·鲍威尔和帕特·麦卡斯克创作的音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德莉创作。

sentences.en: This episode was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的音频工程由艾莉莎·莫克斯利完成。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是蕾切尔·亚伯拉罕斯。

sentences.en: See you on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 周日见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个被严格掌控的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了－批自诩为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》节目中，我和萨拉·科尼格将带您了解那些试图维持影响力却在不知不觉中失去控制的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
